I have been farming in Quzhou since I was a boy. My father taught me, and his father before him. I know this land — the soil, the wells, the seasons. With 3.5 mu I cannot afford mistakes. Let me think through what I will do.

**Wheat and maize** go on 2.5 mu together in rotation — wheat in October after the maize harvest, maize in June right after wheat. This is what everyone here does. It fills the calendar and uses the land twice a year. I will use the improved Jimai wheat variety the township seed station sells — it does well here and I know it. For maize I will buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever the store has that's reputable. I apply urea and compound fertilizer at the rates I have learned over the years. Wheat needs three irrigations — at sowing if the soil is dry, at jointing, and at heading. Maize is summer and the rains help, so two irrigations is usually enough. I spray herbicide once for wheat and watch for aphids in May. For maize I do one round for pests.

**Cotton** gets the remaining 1 mu. Cotton earns more per mu than grain, and I know how to grow it, but it is hard work and the pesticides cost money. I plough that plot in spring, plant hybrid cotton in late April. Cotton needs more spraying — bollworm, aphids, spider mites — I plan for five rounds of pesticide. I irrigate four times through the dry summer months. I apply more potassium with cotton than with grain because the soil here is potassium-hungry and cotton responds well to it.

I do not change what works. I have four people to feed and inputs to pay for. I manage the water carefully — the well is mine but electricity costs are real and I have heard the water level is lower every year.
